title: Remove Supabase, sign-in and error reporting
description: Owner said this app does not use Supabase (local same-screen arena shooter, no accounts). Purge via .agents/skills/loop-plan/references/remove-feature.md: supabase/, @/shared/services/supabaseService, auth that calls it (Google and anonymous sessions), src/features/error-reporting/ and its call in src/App.tsx, plus references in docs, config, env and guidance. Hosting, UI kit and theme stay. Result: landed on this branch (owner consented to the protected-file edits in chat).

title: Remove Supabase from rules, skills and protected configs
description: Follow-up of the Remove Supabase lap. Protected files, ask the owner for consent per edit: .claude/rules (database, cloud-functions, project-specific, api-integration, security, platform, architecture, testing, git-workflow, file-placement), .agents/skills (vendor-supabase.md, signal-adapter.md, onboarding Supabase gate, research-api and others), .gitignore supabase/.temp, eslint.ignores.js, projectStructure.config.cjs supabase entry, .dependency-cruiser.cjs stack-port-supabase, .claude/settings.json mcp entry. Result: landed on this branch (owner consented to the protected-file edits in chat).

title: Configure Supabase
description: Set up the backend: one Supabase project with the auth providers you use enabled, its Site URL set to the app's primary origin, and its URL and publishable key available as VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (local .env, plus the hosting build variables for main and for previews). Before the app has real users, isolate staging from production with a Supabase Branching staging branch or a second project (documentation/DOC_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS.md § Staging backend). Your coding agent lists the exact requirements, checks the result, and tells you what only you can do. For Google sign-in, requirements are in documentation/DOC_SUPABASE_GOOGLE_OAUTH.md. If you explicitly say this app does not use Supabase, Google sign-in, anonymous sessions, or error reporting, the agent offers to delete that code. Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § Shipped integrations and § Configuration tasks gate (Supabase). Result: archived, the owner said this app does not use Supabase (local same-screen game); code removed by the Remove Supabase task.

title: In-app feedback widget
description: A small signed-in feedback form that writes to app_feedback with the page and environment. Depends on: Signals backend task. Result: archived, the owner said this app does not use Supabase (local same-screen game); code removed by the Remove Supabase task.

title: Admin signals view and switch the signal adapter on
description: An admin-only view (role claim) to triage error clusters and feedback, and turn on loop-backlog's signal adapter so open signals become ranked backlog tasks. Depends on: Signals backend, error capture and feedback widget tasks. Result: archived, the owner said this app does not use Supabase (local same-screen game); code removed by the Remove Supabase task.

title: Add a db:push-staging script or fix the adapter reference
description: The signal adapter (.agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/signal-adapter.md) tells the agent to run `pnpm run db:push-staging`, which does not exist. Either add a script that applies supabase/migrations to the staging project with a pinned Supabase CLI (needs project linking, which the owner must set up), or change the adapter to say the connector or CLI applies migrations. Protected file edit: needs owner approval. Context: documentation/DOC_DECISION_LOG.md § signals-backend D8. Result: archived, the owner said this app does not use Supabase (local same-screen game); code removed by the Remove Supabase task.

title: Decide whether the app uses anonymous sign-ins
description: The app asks Supabase for an anonymous session on every visit and Supabase refuses (anonymous_provider_disabled, HTTP 422), twice per page load. Either enable anonymous sign-ins in the project (anonymous users get the authenticated role, so the feedback policy would admit them; review RLS first) or remove the call. Auth permission model: needs an owner decision. Result: archived, the owner said this app does not use Supabase (local same-screen game); code removed by the Remove Supabase task.

title: Define app vision
description: Collaborate with the coding agent to fill documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md (problem, persona, app role). Replace placeholder bullets with real prose and change Vision status from DRAFT to ACTIVE when complete. Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § App vision & goals gate. Result: DOC_APP_VISION.md is ACTIVE, written from the owner game design document (local same-screen arena shooter).

title: Capture app errors to the database
description: Global window error and unhandledrejection handler, error boundary reporting, and the existing logError path, all writing through the deduplicating upsert from the signals backend task. Tag each error with the environment (local, staging, production). Depends on: Signals backend task. Result: merged in PR #28 (src/features/error-reporting; live on production).

title: Signals backend: error logs, feedback and bugs tables
description: Add supabase/migrations with error_logs (clustered by hash, upsert_error_log function), app_feedback and bugs tables, RLS, and a db:push-staging script, so the signal adapter in .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/signal-adapter.md has data to read. Forks get this by default. Admin = a role claim in the user's auth app_metadata (never user_metadata, which users can edit); admins and local dev can read, signed-in users can insert their own rows. Test it on a scratch Postgres, then apply it to the project; with isolated staging, staging first and production after merge. Result: merged in PR #27 (tables, upsert_error_log, RLS; Google sign-in and production build verified; one shared Supabase project by default, D10).

title: Onboarding states requirements, not methods
description: Rewrite the onboarding gates and the seeded Supabase and hosting tasks so they state setup requirements (end state, why, how the agent verifies, who acts) instead of vendor click paths, and add the staging Supabase project requirement. Decisions: documentation/DOC_DECISION_LOG.md § onboarding-requirements. Result: merged in PR #26 (onboarding.md states requirements; Supabase and hosting requirement tables; signals epic queued).

title: Run the loop skill evals against the v0.42.0 baseline
description: Deferred from the skill-loop rework (skill-loop D59) to save usage. Run the eval cases under .agents/skills/router/evals/ and .agents/skills/loop-*/evals/ (15 cases), once with the new skill and once with the v0.42.0 skills it replaced (baseline = commit a920c0d), using the skill-creator workflow or `claude plugin eval`. Report pass rates per skill, and fix the skills where the new version loses behavior. Context: documentation/DOC_DECISION_LOG.md § skill-loop. Result: 45/45 graders passed on new skills vs 39/45 on v0.42.0 baseline (composer-2.5); 0 regressions.

title: Show the harness overview on the app's home page and README
description: Publish the designed harness flowchart as an app route (/harness) built from kit components and the bronze theme tokens, with a PNG preview (public/harness-overview.png). Show a welcome card on the home page so visitors on the preview URL and on a fresh first run see it, and put the image at the top of README.md so people arriving from GitHub or Google see it. Result: merged in PR #32 (src/features/harness-overview, route /harness, public/harness-overview.png).

title: Fix Google sign-in returning to the wrong site with a PKCE error
description: Seen on the production site after signing in with Google from a preview: 'PKCE code verifier not found in storage'. Supabase auth logs show the sign-in started on the preview origin, Supabase redirected to the Site URL (production) because the app's bare-origin redirect address did not match the '/**' allow-list pattern, and production then failed with bad_code_verifier. The app also exchanges the code twice (supabase-js does it during client init, then the callback hook again), which would show a false error even when sign-in works. Decisions: documentation/DOC_DECISION_LOG.md § google-signin-return. Result: merged in PR #29 (0817eac, fix(auth): return Google sign-in to the app root and skip a redundant code exchange).

title: Orchestrator for parallel laps
description: An optional orchestrator role (skill) the owner talks to: it owns the backlog and task state, watches the app vision, runs several laps at once in separate threads, relays questions between threads and the owner, and verifies and merges their work. Backlog/state work moves out of the per-lap loop into it. With one task, the plain loop runs without it. Keep the instructions lean: name outcomes, not procedure.

title: Deny reading nested secrets files
description: Widen .claude/settings.json permissions.deny from root-only ./.env* and ./.dev.vars* to recursive **/ patterns so nested secrets (e.g. supabase/functions/.env) are never read or sent to the model provider; .env.example stays readable via a negated deny rule. From the Claude Code video-lessons review.

title: Replace architecture.md folder tree with pointer and folder meanings
description: The src/ tree in .claude/rules/architecture.md § Folder structure had drifted (listed routes/ store/ lib/ that do not exist, missed whitelisted api/ and shared/config/) and duplicated ARCHITECTURE.md. Replaced with a pointer to ls src/, projectStructure.config.cjs, pnpm validate:structure and ARCHITECTURE.md, keeping four one-line folder meanings the tools cannot express. From the Claude Code video-lessons review (option B, owner-approved).

title: Feedback hooks: lint after edit, type-check before turn end
description: Claude Code hooks replace remember-to-run instructions: a PostToolUse hook runs ESLint --fix on each edited .ts/.tsx file and returns remaining errors to the agent; a Stop hook runs type-check when TypeScript files changed and blocks the turn end once per failing state. Shared hook-input reader in scripts/hook-input.cjs; push-safety.md lint paragraph trimmed. From the Claude Code video-lessons review (owner picked both, Stop hook type-check only).

title: Context-cost audit: slim always-on rules
description: meta-audit-harness context-cost lens (R1-R9): moved Model A/B promote and PR procedures from git-workflow.md into loop-ship references, cut Related Rules footers (DOC_RULES_INDEX is SSOT), moved Windows-only shell text to documentation/DOC_WINDOWS_SHELL.md, and trimmed testing, agent-behavior, code-style and architecture to pointers. Always-on context about 17.6k to 14.5k tokens (-18%), no information lost (ledger in the lap folder). Follow-ups R10-R12 are separate backlog tasks. From the Claude Code video-lessons review.

title: Put your app online (Cloudflare hosting)
description: Get your app live on the internet with Cloudflare (free tier is fine). Your coding agent does the setup — just ask it to "do the hosting task". What you need ready: a Cloudflare account and (optional) a domain name you own. How it works once set up depends on your git workflow mode (see .claude/rules/git-workflow.md § Mode behavior table, rows staging and production) — by default every pull request gets its own preview link and merging the pull request ships to production. One step happens in the Cloudflare website (connecting your repo); the agent tells you what must be set there and why, waits for you, and checks the result. Agent playbook + troubleshooting: documentation/DOC_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS.md (see "Agent one-shot brief"). If you explicitly say this app does not use Cloudflare, the agent offers to delete that hosting code (there is then no preview link). Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § Shipped integrations and § Configuration tasks gate (Hosting). Status: Worker bompers is connected (production https://bompers.tom-fab.workers.dev serves deep links). Preview command must be npx wrangler versions upload; the dashboard default npx wrangler preview (private beta) gave 404 on deep links such as /harness. Open: confirm a branch build with that command serves /harness, then archive.

title: Game engine foundation
description: Blocking for all gameplay tasks. Add pixi.js@8.23.0 (renderer only; orchestrator call, see DOC_APP_VISION.md § Engine). Build the game shell: a canvas page at `/` (replacing the template home), a Pixi lifecycle hook safe under StrictMode, a fixed-timestep loop (e.g. 120 Hz) driving a pure-TS simulation `step(state, inputs, dt)` with no DOM, an input layer for up to 4 players (keyboard for 2 + Gamepad API for 4), a grid-based terrain module (solid/empty cells, collision queries, circle-clear for blasts, chunked redraw), a level data format (platforms, destructible vs solid, spawn points, drop points, out-of-bounds zone) and one tunables/config module (gravity, match duration). A placeholder box per player proves input → sim → render. Writes the module map (feature split per bounded concept, shared engine code) so later threads can work in parallel without overlap. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Player movement and blob feel
description: Depends on: Game engine foundation. Character controller in the sim: smooth accel/decel, curved motion, high jumps scaled by gravity, air steering, wall-jumps, landing squash and foot deform (render side), aim direction per input. Tunables in the config module. Unit tests for the controller. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Multi-target camera
description: Depends on: Game engine foundation. Pure-math camera that frames all active players with zoom limits, smoothing and a central deadzone; applied to the render container. Unit tests. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Level file format and preview kit
description: Not blocked by code (coordinate the data shape with the engine foundation's LevelDefinition + content catalog via the orchestrator). Define the level file: one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG, any AI agent can write it, any browser shows it. Shapes carry data- attributes for role (platform, spawn, drop, bounds, collectible) and references by ID only (material, effect, sound, behaviour). Deliver: documentation/game/LEVEL_FORMAT.md (spec + versioning + migration policy), an agent-ready authoring guide, an example level, and a public level kit (served under /level-kit/v1/: preview stylesheet + small preview script that draws a legend and labels when the file is opened outside the app, and a catalog.json placeholder). A level must still render as a plain picture with no network. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md § Levels.

title: Level importer in the game
description: Depends on: Game engine foundation, Level file format and preview kit. Parse an imported level HTML file into LevelDefinition (rasterise SVG shapes into terrain cells), validate with readable errors, resolve unknown IDs to safe defaults with warnings, run format-version migrations, and offer import by file pick and drag-and-drop. Lives in features/level-file (file I/O) on top of features/level (domain model). Built-in levels are real files in public/levels/. Generate the kit's catalog.json and reference tables from the content catalog in code during the build, with a drift check in CI so the kit stays in sync as the game grows. Also swaps the kit's preview colours to the Gumdrop Pop palette. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md § Levels.

title: Starting arena and destructible terrain
description: Depends on: Game engine foundation, Level importer in the game. Author the start map as the first HTML level file (floating main platform, raised plateaus, open side edges, no hazards; destructible sections, spawn points, drop locations, out-of-bounds bounds) and load it through the importer, proving the format end to end. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md § Levels.

title: Combat: health, hit API, rocket launcher and explosions
description: Depends on: Player movement and blob feel, Starting arena and destructible terrain. 4-chunk health; a zone-aware hit API (front/back damage from tunables, default 1/2) shared by every attack; rocket launcher pickup dropping from the sky; rockets from the helmet in aim direction; explosions remove 1 chunk from hit opponents, push everyone (rocket jumps, no self-damage) and clear terrain cells. The unarmed attack is the separate dive headbutt task. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md. Result: PR #10 (features/combat, applyHit + classifyHitZone, unarmedAttack hook for the dive task).

title: Design language for the game
description: Not blocked by code. Propose 2–3 visual directions for characters (round blob body, two round feet, helmet), arena, UI and effects, plus an audio identity, then the orchestrator picks one. Deliver documentation/game/DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md (palette, shapes, line/shading, motion, UI type, sound direction) and the UI color tokens. ElevenLabs image generation allowed for moodboards within the budget the orchestrator sets. Does not touch game code. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Make the interface yours
description: Everything visible still shows the template. Your coding agent renames the app (browser tab title in index.html, top bar in src/layouts/Topbar/Topbar.tsx), walks through the home page and top bar with you (keep or change each), and removes the harness overview card (src/features/harness-overview/, src/pages/HarnessOverviewPage.tsx and its test, the /harness route in src/App.tsx, the card in src/pages/HomePage.tsx, public/harness-overview.png, plus its README.md image and documentation/DOC_INDEX.md row). Then restyle via the design token files in src/shared/theme/tokens/ and run pnpm tokens:build (documentation/DOC_THEMING.md); verify both modes with the theme icon in the profile menu. It also replaces the template icon and adds your app icons, theme color and link-preview card (title, description, image) in public/ and index.html; you supply a logo or approve a drawn one, and paste your preview link into a chat app to check the card. Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § Configuration tasks gate (Interface). Result: PR #18 — renamed to Bompers, harness overview removed, owner-picked Bomp sky mark (Mascot kept as backup, documentation/game/BRAND.md) as favicon/app icons/manifest and 1200×630 link-preview card; tokens came with the design-language lap (#13).

title: Dive headbutt: unarmed attack
description: Owner pick (2026-11-14): Cannonball launch (wind-up, straight zero-gravity committed dive) plus Pogo's ricochet off other characters only; no bouncing off terrain (keeps it controllable). Keep the slightly unpredictable hit reaction. Plus a shared hurt reaction ('tumble'): hard hits make the VICTIM pogo-bounce off floors and walls, also triggered by strong rocket blasts. Hits go through combat's applyHit (front 1 / back 2, tunable). Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Match rules, scoring and respawn
description: Depends on: Combat. Timed round, points for kills (incl. knock-offs out of bounds) and collectibles falling from the sky, winner screen, respawn at the safe spawn point farthest from opponents with blinking invulnerability and full freedom of action. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Path-scope src-only guidance into its own rule
description: Context-cost audit follow-up (R10): move src-only guidance (architecture code placement and edge-case placement, code-style TypeScript and styling, debugging API troubleshooting) out of always-on rules into a rule with paths: ["src/**"], saving about 1.7k tokens on non-src tasks. Keep the folder meanings in architecture.md § Folder structure. Protected files: owner consent per edit.

title: Trim skill descriptions with trigger tests
description: Context-cost audit follow-up (R11): shorten the .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md descriptions that are listed in every session (about 3.5k tokens; target about -0.8k) and verify with meta-write-skill trigger tests that the right skill still triggers. Protected files: owner consent.

title: Lobby and match settings
description: Depends on: Match rules. Join screen where 1–4 players claim a slot with any keyboard half or gamepad, settings for match duration and gravity, start/restart flow. Replaces the remaining template UI (absorbs the template 'Make the interface yours' work for the game). Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Level picker
description: Let players choose the level before a round: the built-in levels in public/levels/ (start-arena, floating-garden) plus imported ones from the session. Fits the lobby flow. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Let loop skills call Claude Code built-in review skills
description: Context-cost audit follow-up (R12): have loop-check call the built-in /code-review and loop-build or spec-optimize-performance call /simplify instead of duplicating their checks; /loop and /batch do not overlap loop-orchestrate. Protected files: owner consent.

title: Port feedback hooks to Cursor
description: Feedback-hooks follow-up: check the current Cursor hooks docs (afterFileEdit, stop) and port the Claude Code PostToolUse lint/format hook and Stop type-check hook where Cursor supports equivalent behavior; document gaps.

title: Game sound effects
description: Depends on: Design language for the game, Combat. Generate SFX with ElevenLabs (jump, land squish, bash, rocket fire, explosion, pickup, hit, elimination, respawn, round start/end) within the orchestrator's credit budget; small Web Audio playback module driven by sim events. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Apply the design language in game
description: Depends on: Design language for the game, Player movement and blob feel, Starting arena and destructible terrain. Characters, arena, pickups, effects and HUD drawn in the chosen style. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.  Owner picked line style E (silhouette outline only, softer egg-shaped blobs, body gradient + gloss; DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md). Also: fix the PixiJS deprecation (addChild on Graphics in features/player playerRenderer.ts) and load Fredoka before drawing canvas text.

title: Port the no-git-writes-on-main guard to Cursor
description: Harness: Cursor agents should get the same protection as Claude Code. Add a fail-safe beforeShellExecution hook in .cursor/hooks.json mirroring scripts/deny-git-write-on-main (from the Cursor feedback-hooks lap, #20). Owner follow-up from #20: run the Cursor feedback hooks once in a real Cursor session and fix the tool_input field name if the lint error doesn't come back.

title: Move launcher pickups into features/collectibles
description: Code cleanup (combat D2, match-rules follow-up): one home for everything that drops from the sky. Move the rocket-launcher crate spawning/pickup from features/combat into features/collectibles next to point orbs; combat keeps weapons and firing. No behaviour change. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Game feel: hit flash, screen shake, helmet wobble
description: Render-only feedback the visual pass left out: hit flash on the victim's fill (back hits stronger), capped decaying screen shake (explosions, hard dive hits, tumble bounces), helmet spring wobble, render-only hit-stop; feel tunables; prefers-reduced-motion respected. No sim change. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Side and top map edges stop killing players
description: Feedback round 2 § 3. Players die unexpectedly at the sides and top of the map ('killed by the air'). Only the bottom (falling to your death) should feel lethal; sides and top must feel like open space. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md; owner feedback: documentation/game/FEEDBACK_ROUND_2.md.

title: Slower jumps and rocket recoil
description: Feedback round 2 § 3. Jumps are too fast to coordinate trick jumps: lower gravity for more air control, balanced with a lower jump impulse so max height stays sensible. Firing a rocket gives no recoil today: add a physical kick on the shooter (impact and tactical movement, e.g. small rocket-assisted moves). Tunables in gameTunables. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md; owner feedback: documentation/game/FEEDBACK_ROUND_2.md.

title: Music
description: Upbeat ukulele/marimba loops around 128 BPM per DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md § 8 (lobby loop + match loop + short stingers). The audio duck bus is already wired (explosions duck music). Same owner-guided process as the SFX lap; confirm credit cost with the orchestrator before generating long tracks. Add a music volume next to the SFX volume. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.  Also covers the missing end-phase audio (feedback round 2 § 3): a tension loop or stinger for the last 30 seconds of a match.

title: Feet animation: rotation, dynamics and wall-facing feet
description: Feedback round 2 § 2.5 and § 3. The feet only move straight up and down; they lost the rotation, dynamics and feel of the pre-restyle version. Bring back rotation and dynamic motion (earlier ideas like taller sprites or changed collision are dropped). While wall-sliding and wall-jumping, the feet turn to face the wall surface. Render-only. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md; owner feedback: documentation/game/FEEDBACK_ROUND_2.md.

title: Homing missiles (dodgeable)
description: Owner request 2026-11-16. A homing-missile weapon: missiles track a target but are dodgeable, never a guaranteed hit (limited turn rate, lock delay, fuel/lifetime or similar — the lap proposes the dodge rule). Picked up from crates like the rocket launcher. A separate weapon from the normal rocket launcher (owner 2026-11-16): the missile itself looks different — another colour or a red blinking part — and its crate looks different too. Uses the weapon visual system once defined (placeholder until then). Waits on slower jumps and rocket recoil (#31, same rocket code). Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md; juice: documentation/game/GAME_JUICE.md once #34 lands.

title: Crouch: defensive stance
description: Feedback round 2 § 2.4. Holding down puts the blob in a fixed crouch: it cannot walk, sinks to the ground, feet nearly invisible. All incoming damage is halved; attacks or hazards that normally deal 1 damage deal 0. Waits on slower jumps and the feet animation lap (same player code). Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md; owner feedback: documentation/game/FEEDBACK_ROUND_2.md.

title: Finer headbutt directions (16 ways)
description: Owner request 2026-11-16: the headbutt/dive can only aim in 45° steps (diveSim AIM_STEP = π/4, 8 ways); halve it to 22.5° (16 ways). Keyboard aim is 8-way from the keys, so the lap checks how keyboard players reach the in-between angles and asks the owner if a new control scheme is needed. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Game juice design system
description: Feedback round 2 § 4.2. New game elements keep arriving; define one consistent set of constants and guidelines for sounds, squash-and-stretch and visual feedback (extend DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md and the feel tunables; an agent skill or several, the lap decides) so every new element gets the same style and feel. Skill or rule files need the owner's yes. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md; owner feedback: documentation/game/FEEDBACK_ROUND_2.md.

title: Gamepad support and verification
description: The owner has only verified keyboard play. Make up to 4 gamepads work end to end: join, move, aim (stick), jump, fire/dive, hot-plug and disconnect, sensible deadzones; then the owner verifies with real controllers. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Weapon and crate visual design system
description: Owner request 2026-11-16. Design with the owner first, with examples, before building. (1) Crates show what's inside. (2) A visual system for weapons: today every weapon is a tube on the blob's head. Owner idea: replace the figure on the head with the weapon's icon instead of the team; but in team games blob colour identifies the player and the helmet might identify the team — so what identifies the weapon? Define the logic: player = blob colour, team = ?, weapon = ?, consistent across crate, HUD and blob. Build waits on the feet animation lap (same player renderer). Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md; juice: documentation/game/GAME_JUICE.md once #34 lands.

title: Uniform material system for level maps
description: Feedback round 2 § 4.1. Externally generated HTML levels need unambiguous materials. Destructible and indestructible blocks share shape and base structure (the current purple ground) but differ clearly in colour (e.g. cardboard tint for destructible). Add material behaviours such as ice (slippery) and colour variants (ice, earth, cardboard, indestructible). Design question for the lap: decouple physical behaviour from colour (any colour on any behaviour, no LittleBigPlanet-style material explosion) while a player still recognises destructible vs slippery at a glance. No backwards compatibility needed: old levels may break; update the shipped levels, LEVEL_FORMAT.md and the level kit. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md; owner feedback: documentation/game/FEEDBACK_ROUND_2.md.

title: In-game pause menu
description: Feedback round 2 § 2.2. During a match any player can open a pause menu (keyboard and gamepad Start) that fully freezes gameplay. In it: back to main menu, SFX on/off, music on/off, general options. Match settings stay lobby-only. Must open on Escape (owner 2026-11-16) as well as any pad's Start. Gamepad support (#35) and music (#33) are on main. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md; owner feedback: documentation/game/FEEDBACK_ROUND_2.md.

title: Headbutt reset power-up
description: Feedback round 2 § 2.3. A level pickup (Ori-style) that, when flown through mid-air after the headbutt/dive charge is spent, restores the charge immediately so players can chain headbutts without landing. Placeable in levels. Waits on the uniform material system (level format change). Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md; owner feedback: documentation/game/FEEDBACK_ROUND_2.md.

title: Material collision sounds
description: Follow-up from the sound lap: give the terrain materials real impact/destroy sounds (the catalog's thud and crumble are still silent) and use the saved dive-impact spares. Same process as the SFX lap: palette in DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md § 8, small test batch with explicit durations, owner picks on an artifact, then wire through the content catalog (pnpm level-kit:sync). Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.  Waits on the uniform material system. Also run the round-2 audio experiment: swap the headbutt-into-wall sound with the jump-landing sound and let the owner judge which fits.

title: Copyable level-generation prompt
description: Feedback round 2 § 2.1. Next to the 'Your Level' import, a one-click copy button for a standard system prompt the user pastes into an external AI agent (e.g. Gemini) to generate a valid, playable HTML level in one shot: all required constants, variables, entities and material definitions. Owner example prompt (format v1): documentation/game/LEVEL_PROMPT_EXAMPLE.md — sections 1–6 must be generated from the live format, catalog and tunables (the jumps lap changes gravity and jump numbers), section 7 is the user's map request. Owner note: 'only the variable settings in it' (lap clarifies with the owner). Waits on the uniform material system and the headbutt reset power-up so the prompt describes the final format. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md; owner feedback: documentation/game/FEEDBACK_ROUND_2.md.

title: Level import warns on items in the wrong role
description: Follow-up from the headbutt-reset lap: the level importer and the level kit preview warn when an item id is used on the wrong role (e.g. data-item="dive-reset" on a drop, or a weapon id on a collectible), so hand-made and AI-generated levels fail loudly instead of silently. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Material responses: blast power and spreading fire
description: Owner direction 2026-11-16 (supersedes the earlier fire-only scope): one shared model where a source only says WHERE and HOW STRONG, and the material decides the result. (1) Blasts: a rocket picks only its explosion point and power (no fixed crater radius); each material's toughness decides the cutout. Blast power also drives the push on players (owner 2026-11-16): one scalable blast power from 0 (barely moves a player) through a small shove to sending them flying, so each weapon is tuned by its blast power alone. (2) Fire: a fire source at a point; fire spreads per tick outward in a circle from the origin, and each material decides whether and how it burns — so part of a block can burn while the rest does not (the terrain cell grid makes that per-cell, not a split entity). (3) A flamethrower weapon. (4) A hit reaction when a blob touches fire. Design with the owner, with examples, before building. Laps: blast-by-power refactor first, then fire + burn reaction, then flamethrower. Build waits on the uniform material system (#36). Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md. Owner 2026-11-16: the material system (#36) is fine but its destructibility must match this paradigm — the breakable flag becomes toughness (stone/ice unbreakable), shared by level format, kit, catalog and the generation prompt.

title: Smooth destruction: Worms / LittleBigPlanet-style terrain
description: Owner request 2026-11-16: destruction must not look or feel restricted to blocks (today: Minecraft/Terraria-like stepped craters on the 8-unit cell grid). Craters and explosions get custom, smooth shapes, like Worms or LittleBigPlanet, and terrain reads as one sheet rather than cells. Owner picked (2026-11-16, after an A-vs-vector deep dive): a fine true-distance field (~4 units) with a truly curved edge (spline or shader), collision and fire on the same field, craters per sample by toughness with custom shapes per weapon; untouched authored shapes may stay sharp. Owned by the blast-power thread (same terrain code); build after the material system (#36) and the blast-power lap. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md. Laps (blast-power thread, D18–D19): a2 distance field + crater on the field, a2r curved edge renderer (shader-vs-spline spike first), a3 collision on the field; after blast power (a); fire (b) after a2r; Shared roll after a3.

title: Fire and flamethrower visuals
description: Owner 2026-11-17: 'Fire visuals looked shit on my last test. I didn't see examples yet of the flamethrower visuals. Need a full lap for those.' Redesign the look of terrain fire (flames on burning cardboard, spread front, burn-out, scorch, smoke), the torch/flamethrower spray and nozzle, and blobs on fire (#55 look kept unless the owner says otherwise). Options page first (loop-refine step 6), owner picks, then build. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; look: documentation/game/DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md; juice: documentation/game/GAME_JUICE.md.

title: Shared roll: dash-hold roll and hit tumble
description: Owner request 2026-11-16: one shared rolling system for all player rolling. (1) Holding the dash button after a dash makes the blob keep rolling. (2) Being hit or launched by a blast uses the same roll, with or without damage. (3) Consolidate: find every existing system that rolls, tumbles or bounces the player (tumble state, dive bonk, body collisions, blast push, landing squash) and fold them into this one roll, removing the duplicates. (4) Real rolling physics: in roll mode the blob actually rolls — on a slope it rolls down the hill, with ground contact, friction and spin. (5) Roll intensity follows the blast power (see Material responses: 0 = barely moves, small = a little shove, strong = flying), so weapons are tuned by blast power. Today a separate tumble state starts only above a fixed impulse threshold (gameTunables player.tumble.minImpulse 800) — replace the threshold with the continuous scale. Waits on the blast-power lap of Material responses and the collision-on-field lap (a3) of Smooth destruction and the headbutt 16-ways PR (#37, same dive code). Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Elimination: ragdoll and fall apart
description: Owner request 2026-11-16: when a blob is lethally hit it ragdolls, or falls apart into pieces that ragdoll; the pieces then blink until they disappear, and the player respawns. Design first: an artifact with live examples of the options before the owner picks. Fills the game-juice gap 'elimination has sound but no visual'. Relates to the Shared roll lap (ragdoll/tumble state) and the loose-parts idea (falling bodies). Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md; juice: documentation/game/GAME_JUICE.md.

title: Legs: one system for wall and slope
description: Owner request 2026-11-17: leg animation from wall walk and arced slope walk should transition nicely or be one system. Owner picked B, one surface frame (PR #59). Planted feet (C) parked in the player README.

title: Moving parts in levels
description: Owner request 2026-11-17 (full lap): level parts can rotate and move, and the level builder (format, importer, level kit preview, Copy AI prompt) supports them. Must be easy for an agent that only has the level-builder prompt to author correctly and align shapes without seeing them (e.g. anchors, pivots, relative/snap coordinates, named groups). Keep the prompt and format token-light. Cover second-order effects: players/crates/pickups riding and being pushed or crushed by moving parts, collision against moving geometry vs the static distance field, destructibility and fire on moving parts, camera bounds, spawn safety, homing/rockets, determinism, validation warnings, performance. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; level format: documentation/game/LEVEL_FORMAT.md.

title: Ice element
description: Owner request 2026-11-18: do for each element what was done for fire, one by one: a weapon/projectile, an effect on blobs, and an effect per map material (stone, earth, cardboard, ice), plus element interactions (ice puts out fire, fire melts ice). Ice is next; after it lands the owner decides whether another element follows. Starts with an ideation options page (loop-refine step 6). Shared spread/material mechanism named by role, not after fire (code-style F1/F2). Thread: Ice element (Fable).

title: Weapon visuals: embellish
description: Owner 2026-11-16 signed off the weapon and crate visual system (#38) as a work in progress: 'we will embellish further later on'. Polish pass on crates, helmet tubes, muzzle lights and HUD ammo once the owner names what to improve. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md.

title: Fire and ice follow the terrain shape
description: Owner 2026-11-18: burning and frozen areas lose the base shape (per-row rounded slabs). Owner picked C: draw states with the same contour rule as the terrain (terrainContour region option replacing breakableOnly, a sample-region field, surface points). Fire and ice renderers switch over after the freeze ray (#63) merges. Thread: Fire and ice overlays keep the terrain shape.

title: Stains as a terrain state
description: Owner 2026-11-18: goo splats should stain the actual objects (the samples/texels of terrain and moving parts) instead of drawing a sprite on top. Use the same per-sample state system as fire and ice (a third state with a colour per stain and fading), drawn through the region/contour mechanism, including on moving parts. Starts with an options page. After the fire and ice overlay-shape lap.

title: Weapons as a match setting
description: Level direction (owner 2026-11-18, PR #61 D1–D8): lobby setting like match duration; auto = every weapon the game has (old maps get new weapons); a level may state a default (e.g. only rockets, no weapons). Remove data-items from drops in format, importer, kit, prompt and built-in levels (format change; compatibility waived). Size S–M.

title: Ice lap 2: frozen blobs
description: Ice element follow-up (owner pick 2026-11-18: freeze ray on the fire system, PR #63): frozen blobs and counterplay with crouch, dive and jump. Touches the player feature through overlays and the shared roll; starts with an options page. Size M.

title: Remember a level by file location
description: Level direction (owner 2026-11-18, PR #61 D1–D8): owner idea: keep a level by its file location instead of a stored copy. Research first: a web page cannot store a path; needs the browser File System Access API (not in every browser). Size S.

title: Forgiving level import
description: Level direction (owner 2026-11-18, PR #61 D1–D8): turn each rejection the game can survive into a warning with a fallback (pass over E1–E8 in LEVEL_FORMAT § 7); reject only what the game cannot run. Size S.

title: Copy import report
description: Level direction (owner 2026-11-18, PR #61 D1–D8): lobby button copies the remaining import errors and warnings as plain text so an authoring agent can read them. Size S.

title: Controller focus highlight in menus
description: Owner 2026-11-18 (for later): in the UI, a controller (gamepad) needs a visible highlight on the active UI element, but mouse/keyboard on PC does not. Show the focus highlight only while the last input came from a pad (input-modality detection, like :focus-visible), across lobby rows (incl. the weapons crate cursor from #68 and the level strip), pause menu and other menus. Visible UI change: options page first.

title: Fire and torch sounds
description: Follow-up from fire b1 (#53): the torch start and burn-outs reuse placeholder sounds (rocket-fire, cardboard thwap). Generate real takes (torch whoosh/loop, crackle, burn-out) per DESIGN_LANGUAGE § 8 incl. 'Owner listens first' (artifact page, owner picks before wiring); credits need the owner's go. Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md.

title: Beam clash: torch meets freeze ray
description: Owner 2026-11-18: beams of opposing elements react where they meet instead of overlapping. Owner picked A, steam wall (PR #75): both stop at the meeting point in steam. One beam-vs-beam rule with a pair table.

title: Bug: collision sound retriggers rapidly
description: Owner 2026-11-18, found while playing: in some positions (against a moving platform, or other platforms) the player collision/land sound replays rapidly in bursts. Suspect the sim grounded/airborne flip (#59 found it) and resting/pushed contacts with movers. Fix at the source plus a per-body re-trigger guard.

title: Ability challenge levels
description: Owner 2026-11-18: a creative thread designs levels that challenge every character ability (movement, headbutt, roll, crouch, moving parts) plus weapon abilities and combinations; concepts page first, then authored as kit levels via LEVEL_PROMPT with feedback on the prompt. Built as five built-in levels in PR #79.

title: Level prompt: crusher wording
description: LEVEL_PROMPT section 3 says moving parts keep an 8-unit margin; the importer accepts flush contact and crush needs a gap under 5.6 (crusher-test-level contradicts the prompt). Fix the wording. Size XS. Owner OK 2026-11-18; also add movement numbers at base settings (jump height, running jump, dive length, wall-jump, jump+dive reach) instead of a route checker. Done in PR #79.

title: Double jump bash
description: Owner 2026-11-18: a double jump (mid-air jump) performs the bash, so armed players can bash too. Rule variants on an options page first; controller edits wait for the collision-sound fix.

title: Roll speed carries into jump and dive
description: Owner go 2026-11-18: a jump or dive out of a roll keeps the roll speed. Built in the Double jump bash lap.

title: Squish keeps the eyes
description: Owner 2026-11-18: when a blob is squished everything squashes except the eyes, which keep their size; the eyes switch to the burning-blob panic emotion while squeezed/crushed.

title: Moving parts: materials, fire, ice and beams
description: Owner 2026-11-18: spray beams (torch, freeze ray) must be stopped by moving parts, and moving parts can be any material, so they catch fire or freeze when their material takes it. Owner wants approaches, each deeper than the last, for a very extensible system; design page first. L1 (beams stop on parts) merged in #77.

title: World of bodies L2a: fire on moving parts
description: Body list as state; fire per body; torch lights parts; burn-out cuts the part (outline, collision, drawing follow); blobs catch from a burning part; W13 + LEVEL_FORMAT 11 + prompt line. Owner 2026-11-18: a fully burnt part leaves nothing for the rest of the round (same rule as terrain). Size M.

title: World of bodies L2b: cold on moving parts
description: Freeze ray freezes parts, grip per sample on a part, frozen overlay on parts, thaw, torch thaws parts. Size S-M.

description: Found in world-of-bodies L2a: the fire and arena features are at their 10-files-per-layer budget. Move burning blobs (burningBlobs + blobFireRenderer) into their own feature before L3 adds to fire. Behaviour-neutral refactor. Size S.

title: World of bodies L5: fire crosses where bodies touch

Absorbs the pillar/slab seam look. Owner looks at a junction-lip options page before build. Size M. Thread: outline-system.

title: Loose terrain falls
description: Owner idea 2026-11-16 (future, not scheduled): terrain cut off from its support by a blast or burnt-out fuel breaks loose and falls. On the distance field: flood-fill the touched region for islands not connected to anchored material or the level edge, lift each island out as a contour polygon into a falling body (simple custom body or a physics library — a new dependency is an owner choice), and stamp it back into the field when it settles; falling chunks can hit players. Precedent: Noita (pixel islands become rigid bodies). Waits on the distance field (a2) and collision on the field (a3). Game design SSOT: documentation/game/GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md; product reading: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md. Note from the distance-field lap (#45): only unbreakable samples and the bottom row are anchored, so all-breakable floating platforms have no anchor — this lap needs its own rule for which piece stays put.
